title: iPhone Auto FPS in Low Light and 30 FPS Editing
description: Learn why iPhone Auto FPS can change low-light capture and how to test a steady 30 FPS export before adding the footage to a 30 FPS edit.
direct: If an iPhone clip shot in low light behaves differently in a 30 FPS edit, check the original clip’s frame rate. If the editor needs a steady 30 FPS file, test one converted copy before processing the rest.
figureAlt: A dim indoor camera setup and a strip of frames beside a laptop editing timeline.
figureCaption: AI illustration of low-light capture and editing. It does not show measured frame timing.
cards.decision.heading: Check the clip you already have
cards.decision.body: On supported iPhones, Auto FPS can reduce the capture rate in low light. The camera setting you see today does not tell you the timing of a clip you recorded yesterday.
sections.detail-1.heading: Decide if the extra export helps
sections.detail-1.body: If the original plays correctly and your editor handles it as expected, you may be able to edit it directly. A 30 FPS output can repeat or discard frames. It cannot add moments the camera missed, and fast movement can still look uneven.
sections.detail-2.heading: Separate capture from delivery
sections.detail-2.body: For future recordings, review Auto FPS under Camera recording settings if you need more consistent capture. Try a short low-light test with your chosen setting. Space Sheep Studio develops VideoFix for iPhone. It offers steady frame-rate exports and keeps the source. See the App Store for current access options.

steps.step-1.text: Check the clip’s video information and play a section with movement and clear speech. Keep the original as a reference.
steps.step-2.text: If your editor needs a steady 30 FPS input, select the 30 FPS frame-rate output in VideoFix: HDR Video Converter and export one copy.
steps.step-3.text: Import the copy into the same timeline. Check a moving subject and compare dialogue near the beginning and end. Check color if the source is HDR and the copy is SDR.
